trigger_condition: Run invoked for a company with zero active employees
guard_snippet: if (activeEmployees.length === 0) return run with zero payslips + 'no employees' status, not an error
potential_consequence: Run crashes or half-created payroll_run row with no defined terminal state

trigger_condition: Employee in run scope has no salary structure effective for that month
guard_snippet: skip employee with 'no salary structure' flag on run summary; never emit a zero-gross payslip silently
potential_consequence: Employee silently paid zero, or run aborts for all employees over one gap

trigger_condition: Employee has no attendance records at all for the run month
guard_snippet: define: no rows = all-absent LOP vs excluded-from-run; summariseEmployeeMonth must state empty-grid semantics
potential_consequence: Full-month LOP deducted from an employee who was simply never enrolled

trigger_condition: Cut-off day set to 0, 32, or a value after month end (29/30/31 in Feb)
guard_snippet: validate cutOffDay in 1..31 with per-month clamping or rejection of >28 for Feb
potential_consequence: Run window resolves to an invalid date; attendance slice undefined or crashes

trigger_condition: Cut-off day set after the pay date's month boundary or after month end
guard_snippet: validate cutoff < monthEnd and cutoff <= payDate-1 with plain-English rejection
potential_consequence: Run counts attendance into a month whose payroll already paid out

trigger_condition: Join date >= exit date, or join date equals exit date (same-day employment)
guard_snippet: if (effectiveTo < effectiveFrom) reject employee with data-error flag; zero-day window yields zero payable days, not divide-by-zero
potential_consequence: Negative payable days or division producing negative/NaN daily wage

trigger_condition: Approved leave range spans the month boundary of the run
guard_snippet: state: per-date leave rows split by run month; each month's run counts only its own days
potential_consequence: Both months charge the full leave, or neither does

trigger_condition: Leave days falling before the join date or after exit date within the run month
guard_snippet: exclude leave days outside the employment window from LOP; flag the overlap
potential_consequence: LOP deducted for days the employee was not yet or no longer employed

trigger_condition: Off-cycle payout requested for a month that is already locked
guard_snippet: reject off-cycle lines into locked months with 'locked — use a later month' error
potential_consequence: Off-cycle line mutates or regenerates a frozen payslip, breaking immutability

trigger_condition: Off-cycle line added for a month with no payroll run yet
guard_snippet: define: line is staged and appears when that month runs, or adding it requires a prior run
potential_consequence: Bonus vanishes (no payslip exists) or silently triggers an unrequested run

trigger_condition: Off-cycle earning present when statutory PF/TDS basis is computed
guard_snippet: state explicitly whether off-cycle lines join the PF/TDS basis or are excluded
potential_consequence: Payslip gross/net include the bonus but statutory figures ignore it — self-inconsistent slip

trigger_condition: Two admins run the same unlocked month concurrently
guard_snippet: serialize runs per (tenant, month) with the existing advisory-lock idiom (attendance_lock_tenant precedent)
potential_consequence: Interleaved replace/insert yields duplicate payslips or a mixed-generation month

trigger_condition: Lock commits while another admin's run is still in flight
guard_snippet: run must re-check lock under the same lock guard before its final commit; lock blocks in-flight runs
potential_consequence: Fresh payslips written into a month the admin believes is frozen

trigger_condition: Component deactivated mid-month; an employee structure still references it
guard_snippet: define: run skips deactivated component and flags the employee, or deactivation is blocked while referenced
potential_consequence: Earnings line drops out of gross silently or run errors mid-batch

trigger_condition: Formula references a component the employee's structure carries no amount for, or a deactivated one
guard_snippet: cycle check must extend to missing-operand and inactive-operand resolution per employee at run time
potential_consequence: Null/undefined operand coerced to 0 or NaN in gross

trigger_condition: Payable days exceed the divisor (31-day month, 27 working days, fixed-26 convention)
guard_snippet: cap payable days at the divisor or define the over-divisor arithmetic per convention
potential_consequence: Pay exceeds full monthly gross; or negative remainder treated as recoverable LOP

trigger_condition: Total deductions reach or exceed the 50% cap, including admin-overridden amounts
guard_snippet: cap check must run after overrides; state whether an override above the cap is refused or clamped
potential_consequence: Override bypasses the statutory cap or net pay goes negative

trigger_condition: Heavy LOP plus flat heads drives net pay negative before any cap
guard_snippet: define negative-net handling: clamp at zero with carry-forward note, never emit a negative payslip
potential_consequence: Payslip prints a negative net; recovery path undefined

trigger_condition: Day is half_day (attendance override/corrected) rather than half_day_leave
guard_snippet: state explicitly which of half_day and half_day_leave count as 0.5 LOP
potential_consequence: Corrected half-days silently excluded from or double-counted in LOP

trigger_condition: Day status is checkout_missing for a worked day
guard_snippet: map checkout_missing to a defined payroll treatment (paid pending correction / LOP) in the run contract
potential_consequence: Blocker-flagged days fall into an undefined branch of LOP arithmetic

trigger_condition: Month/cut-off boundary evaluated in server UTC vs tenant timezone
guard_snippet: state: run window, cut-off and pay date resolve in the tenant timezone
potential_consequence: Day-status rows straddle the month edge inconsistently between payroll and attendance views

trigger_condition: Two structure revisions share an effective month, or effective date falls mid-month
guard_snippet: define pick rule (later revision wins; effective dates must align to month start or explicit mid-month rule)
potential_consequence: Run selects an arbitrary revision; re-run produces different numbers

trigger_condition: TDS slab estimate computed with no prior months of earnings data (first run, mid-FY joiner)
guard_snippet: define annualization: project from month-one or month-of-join basis; state the regime-restart rule
potential_consequence: First-month TDS wildly off; wrong slab applied to the annual projection

trigger_condition: Re-run replaces payslips while a prior month's PDF is queued or already downloaded
guard_snippet: define: regenerating supersedes queued PDF requests; old presigned URLs invalidated or versioned
potential_consequence: Employee downloads a stale superseded payslip after the numbers changed

trigger_condition: PDF generation fails after the month is locked
guard_snippet: define post-lock PDF retry path that regenerates the file only, never recomputes amounts
potential_consequence: Employee permanently unable to download their locked month's payslip

trigger_condition: Run for a past month before payroll existed, or a future month whose cut-off has not occurred
guard_snippet: validate run month: not before company payroll start, not beyond the current cut-off
potential_consequence: Backdated run picks up absent historical config; future run pays unworked days

trigger_condition: Paid-type half-day leave taken within entitlement — 0.5 rule vs beyond-entitlement rule conflict
guard_snippet: state precedence: within-entitlement paid leave (incl. half-days) yields no LOP; 0.5 applies to unpaid/overflow days
potential_consequence: Half of an entitled paid leave deducted as LOP, contradicting CAP-12's fixture

trigger_condition: Leave type reclassified after a run but before lock, then month re-run
guard_snippet: state whether reclassification applies on re-run of a prior unlocked month or only months after the change date
potential_consequence: Re-run flips LOP for a closed attendance period with no audit boundary

location: Constraints (employment dates are new schema data)
trigger_condition: Membership removed mid-month but no exit date captured
guard_snippet: define fallback: memberships.status change date used when exit date absent, or run flags employee for manual exit date
potential_consequence: Proration cannot resolve; employee paid a full month after removal

trigger_condition: Flat monthly head applied to an employee prorated to a partial month
guard_snippet: state whether flat heads are also prorated by payable days or always charged in full
potential_consequence: Full PT charged on a half-month's pay, blowing past the 50% cap

location: CAP-1 (success: renaming reflected, history keeps name)
trigger_condition: Component renamed between run and re-run of the same unlocked month
guard_snippet: state which name a regenerated payslip in an unlocked month carries (current vs run-date snapshot)
potential_consequence: Re-run produces different slip labels, breaking the 'same numbers until config changes' promise

trigger_condition: Off-cycle bonus inflates wage-period gross, changing the cap denominator mid-month
guard_snippet: define the cap basis explicitly: includes or excludes off-cycle lines in wage-period gross
potential_consequence: Cap enforcement differs between the run and the off-cycle path

location: Constraints — Legal basis bullet (no matching CAP)
trigger_condition: The flat 50% total-deduction cap (LOP included) and the excess-recovery path exist only as a constraint sentence — no capability, no run-time behaviour, and no success test owns them.
guard_snippet: Extend CAP-6's success: 'A fixture whose computed deductions (PF + TDS + PT + LOP) exceed 50% of the wage base is capped at 50% and a recovery line is raised for the excess, surfacing on the next run's payslip.' Without a success assertion, the constraint is unbuildable-by-contract.
potential_consequence: The single load-bearing compliance rule from the statutory digest (Q4 'CHANGES DESIGN') never gets built or tested; a run silently over-deducts past the legal cap and the excess-recovery path it promises does not exist.

trigger_condition: '50% total-deduction cap per wage period, LOP included' never defines the cap base — gross before or after the LOP reduction, and whether employer contributions count toward the cap.
guard_snippet: State the base: 'Cap base = wages payable for the period (gross after LOP reduction, before all deductions); employer PF/ESI shares sit outside the cap.'
potential_consequence: Two implementations one interpretation apart produce different net pay for the same fixture, and the QA engineer cannot write the boundary test without guessing which base the law means.

trigger_condition: 'A simple new-regime TDS slab estimate' specifies no slab data, no annualization convention, no month-spread rule, and its success test asserts only that TDS appears on the payslip — never any amount.
guard_snippet: Pin the semantics: 'TDS estimate = new-regime slab table (effective-dated config) applied to annualized projected salary (current monthly gross × 12, standard deduction applied) ÷ 12.' Add a success fixture asserting the exact rupee instalment for basic ₹20,000.
potential_consequence: Each story implements a different plausible estimate (per-month slab vs annualized), TDS drifts across the year with nothing to catch it, and s.192 under-deduction liability (statutory digest Q7, unverified) lands on the employer with Fenzit as the calculator.

trigger_condition: Auto-PF '12% of basic, cap-aware' has no applicability rule — no covered-employee threshold, no explicit ₹15,000 ceiling fixture, and no way to switch PF off for a company below the EPF threshold.
guard_snippet: Add: 'Auto-PF applies only when the company marks itself PF-covered (company-level switch, default on).' Extend success: 'fixture basic ₹20,000 → 12% of the ₹15,000 ceiling = ₹1,800 (employee share only, on the payslip).'
potential_consequence: A company under the EPF threshold gets statutory contributions it does not owe, and the cap arithmetic — the one genuinely interesting boundary — ships with no test.

trigger_condition: The intent says LOP 'derives from leaves beyond paid entitlement' but the success fixture derives LOP purely from unpaid-typed leaves — and no entitlement or leave-balance model exists in any CAP.
guard_snippet: Resolve to one rule in both intent and success — simplest per the keep-it-simple direction: 'LOP = approved leaves of unpaid-marked types; paid-typed leaves are never LOP regardless of balance (no accrual engine in v1).' Add the boundary fixture: a paid-typed leave with an exhausted balance.
potential_consequence: The two halves of the same CAP disagree; the builder picks one silently, and paid-leave-overrun either becomes free paid time or an unplanned accrual/balance engine enters the epic.

trigger_condition: Only leave requests feed LOP; an employee absent with no leave request (day-status absent) and checkout_missing days have no defined pay treatment.
guard_snippet: Add one line to the invariants: 'LOP counts approved unpaid leaves AND day-status absent days with no leave request; checkout_missing is LOP until corrected through the existing owner-correction path (which the run re-consumes).'
potential_consequence: A no-show employee who never applies for leave is paid in full — the exact loss the feature exists to stop — and the spec's own Why paragraph (attendance-linked LOP) is quietly narrower than attendance.

trigger_condition: The cut-off defines what a run counts 'only up to' — but attendance and leaves between the cut-off (default 25th) and month-end are owned by no run at all.
guard_snippet: State the carry-over: 'Attendance/leaves after the cut-off in month M are counted in month M+1's run as prior-period days, and the payslip lists them under that month.' Add a fixture: a leave on the 27th appears in next month's run.
potential_consequence: Roughly six days of every month are silently neither paid nor LOP'd anywhere — a systematic per-month under/over-payment no fixture can catch because the spec never states the rule.

location: CAP-3 / Constraints — Runs are idempotent per month
trigger_condition: Nothing defines run atomicity, whether a run is a synchronous request or an async job, or what happens when two admins run the same tenant-month concurrently (code audit: no month-level lock precedent exists).
guard_snippet: Add: 'A run is atomic per tenant-month — a failed run leaves zero payslips, never a partial month; concurrent runs for the same month serialize via the existing advisory-lock idiom; the run is an async operation with a status the admin polls.'
potential_consequence: A crash, timeout, or double-click mid-run leaves half the company paid and half not with no record of which, and 're-running replaces cleanly' cannot be honoured over a partial state.

trigger_condition: The run computes 'each employee's pay' but an employee with no salary structure — never configured, or no structure effective for that month — has undefined behaviour.
guard_snippet: Add: 'Employees without an effective structure for the run month are skipped and listed in the run summary as not-configured; the run never emits a ₹0 payslip silently.'
potential_consequence: A forgotten employee receives a statutory wage slip asserting ₹0 earnings — a legally meaningful artefact produced by omission — or the run 500s on the first such employee and stalls.

location: CAP-10 — Off-cycle payout / Constraints — Locked history
trigger_condition: CAP-10 permits an off-cycle 'in a chosen month' with no stated relation to lock; the constraints imply locked-month off-cycles are barred (corrections go 'in a later month'), yet no success tests the rejection — and whether an off-cycle is its own payslip or a line on the next run is undefined.
guard_snippet: Extend CAP-10's success: 'An off-cycle targeting a locked month is rejected with a clear error; an off-cycle renders as its own payslip/credit line for the chosen month and never re-opens a locked month's payslip.'
potential_consequence: The one correction path the spec offers for post-lock mistakes is undefined at precisely its edge case, so an admin with a wrong locked payslip has no working remedy in the built product.

location: CAP-9 — Payroll lock / CAP-7 — Statutory payslip
trigger_condition: Nothing says when a payslip becomes employee-visible (at generation or only after lock), and regeneration 'replaces' payslips with no slip-number uniqueness rule and no lifecycle for the superseded R2 PDF the employee may already hold.
guard_snippet: Decide and state both: 'Payslips become employee-visible only after the month is locked (admin previews pre-lock); each payslip carries a unique immutable slip number (per-tenant sequence, per-month reset); regeneration invalidates the prior PDF's presigned URL and increments the slip number.'
potential_consequence: An employee downloads and keeps a provisional payslip whose numbers the admin then changes by re-running — two legitimate-looking documents for the same month, the classic salary-dispute trigger.

location: CAP-3 vs CAP-5 — proration formula vs LOP-deduction formula
trigger_condition: CAP-3 prorates as payable-days × daily wage (divisor-based), while CAP-5's fixture implies a deduction model (monthly − LOP days × daily). For a join-on-the-2nd with one LOP day in a 31-day month these give 30/26 vs 25/26 of monthly gross — an 11% disagreement, both implied by the same spec.
guard_snippet: Pick one arithmetic and write it as the invariant: 'Monthly pay = monthly gross − (LOP days + 0.5 × half-days) × daily wage, with prorated monthly gross for partial months = (payable days ÷ divisor) × monthly gross only when joining/exiting; LOP then subtracts from the prorated figure.' Add the join-on-2nd-with-LOP fixture.
potential_consequence: The spec's own success criterion ('matches manual calculation') is unfalsifiable — the manual calculation depends on which formula the implementer assumed, and every company's run disagrees with every other implementation of the same spec.

trigger_condition: The formula grammar (operators, references, percentages), money precision (paisa vs rupee), and rounding order are unspecified — the research itself flags rounding order as 'a design decision to make explicitly', and the spec does not make it.
guard_snippet: Add: 'Formulas support component references, constants, + − × ÷ and percent-of only; all money is numeric(18,2); rounding is half-up to the paisa applied once at the final net line, never per component.'
potential_consequence: Per-component rounding vs final-only rounding produces paisa-level mismatches between fixtures and runs across stories, and deactivated-source-component formulas (CAP-1 deactivation × CAP-2 formula) have undefined run behaviour.

trigger_condition: Structure changes carry 'an effective date' and revisions are 'effective from a given month', while joins/exits are day-granular — the granularity of an effective date and mid-month revision behaviour are unstated.
guard_snippet: State it: 'Effective dates are stored day-granular but a run uses the structure in force on the 1st of the run month; a mid-month revision takes effect from the next run' (deliberately no half-month apportionment — that is enterprise-HRMS complexity the user excluded).
potential_consequence: A structure revised on the 15th resolves differently in every implementation — either an unplanned half-month blend engine or a silent whole-month rule nobody specified.

trigger_condition: Auto-proration depends on joining/exit dates, but no capability covers entering them — the code audit confirms no date_of_joining/exit exists on any table and ~842 existing users have neither.
guard_snippet: Add a CAP: 'Company admin sets joining/exit dates per membership in the web admin; existing active memberships are backfilled (admin-supplied or created_at-derived default); a run skips-with-warning any employee whose joining date is missing.'
potential_consequence: CAP-3's headline feature reads a field no story creates — the epic either stalls on an unowned prerequisite at build time or prorates everyone from a null default.

trigger_condition: The mandated field list requires PAN (and designation), but no PAN or designation data exists anywhere in the schema and no CAP collects it — every real payslip fails the CAP's own 'carries every statutory field' success test.
guard_snippet: Extend the employment-data CAP: 'PAN (validated format) and designation are captured on the employee profile in the web admin; a run reports per-employee field-completeness gaps and the payslip renders a missing PAN as blank with an admin-visible warning rather than a fabricated value.'
potential_consequence: The epic discovers at story time that a statutorily complete payslip cannot be rendered from existing data, and a makeshift placeholder (blank, dash, or masked UUID) ships onto a legal document.

trigger_condition: The run's employee population is undefined: memberships include company admins/owners, removed members, and users without attendance enrolment.
guard_snippet: Add: 'A run covers memberships active at the run date with role in the employee set; owners/admins and removed members are excluded unless explicitly configured in; non-enrolled memberships are skipped with a warning.'
potential_consequence: The company owner appears on their own payroll run (and inside PF/TDS arithmetic) by accident, or a recently removed leaver silently drops out of the month they actually worked.

trigger_condition: Lock is stated as a one-way action with no unlock, no stated permanence, and no recovery for an accidental lock other than the off-cycle workaround in a later month.
guard_snippet: State the door explicitly: 'Lock is permanent by design — there is no unlock in v1; a mistaken lock is corrected only via off-cycle payout in a later month (constraint cross-reference), and the admin UI says so at the lock confirmation.'
potential_consequence: An admin who locks the wrong month assumes a fix exists, finds none, and the support answer ('wait for next month's off-cycle') contradicts the product's own error copy.

trigger_condition: The legal-basis bullet adopts CoW timelines as design drivers, yet CoW s.17(2)'s F&F-within-2-working-days obligation for exiting employees is silently absorbed into a non-goal — the leaver's final payslip waits for the normal month-end run.
guard_snippet: Add one honesty line to Assumptions: 'Leaver final pay is issued on the normal monthly run for their exit month; the s.17(2) two-working-day F&F timeline is a documented v1 divergence, accepted pre-launch.'
potential_consequence: The spec claims CoW compliance while a non-goal contradicts it — the divergence surfaces post-launch as a legal finding rather than a recorded, accepted product decision.

trigger_condition: Four capabilities verify money amounts by 'matches manual calculation on the same fixture', but the SPEC defines no canonical fixture — no named employees, no exact attendance/leave rows, no deduction heads, no expected-numbers table; CAP-4's 'same fixture' is literally untestable.
guard_snippet: Add a fixture appendix the tests import verbatim (tenant TZ, month, employee A with basic ₹20,000, HRA 40% basic, divisor fixed-26, PT flat ₹200, 2 paid + 3 unpaid leaves, one half-day, weekly offs per engine) plus an expected-numbers table; reword each success to 'matches the canonical fixture's expected-numbers table'.
potential_consequence: Each story invents its own fixture; no test can fail on cross-capability arithmetic — the exact seam the product sells (attendance → LOP → payslip) stays unverified; real-DB journey tests (test/attendance-journey.e2e-spec.ts precedent: API step + DB as referee) need exact expected rows.
consumer: payroll journey/acceptance tests each CAP story must write; the real-DB journey suite precedent
evidence: SPEC.md CAP-2/3/4/12 all say 'fixture' with different ad-hoc values; no fixture section exists; journey suite asserts exact rows

trigger_condition: Net is asserted but not computable: 'PF 12% of basic, cap-aware' never says which side is deducted (employee 12% reduces net; employer 12% must not), and the TDS estimate gives no annualization method (×12? YTD cumulative? rebate/surcharge/rounding?).
guard_snippet: State: 'PF deducted from employee = 12% of min(basic, PF wage ceiling); employer share recorded, not deducted' and 'TDS = slab(monthly gross × 12 annualized, new regime, minus standard deduction and s.87A rebate, ÷ 12)' with a fixture expected value (expect(payslip.deductions.pf_employee).toBe(1800)).
potential_consequence: The payslip net — the single number every payslip exists to carry — has no defined expected value; an implementation deducting both PF shares (24%) passes every acceptance while shorting every employee.
consumer: CAP-6 acceptance and every downstream net-math test (CAP-3 net, CAP-10 gross/net)
evidence: SPEC.md CAP-6; research dim 1 net formula leaves EPF ambiguity; statutory digest Q7/Q8 mark TDS and PF unverified

trigger_condition: A percentage head on basis 'CTC' has no monthly semantics (CTC is annual per research dim 1), and no basis says whether the percentage applies to full component amount or post-LOP payable amount.
guard_snippet: State: 'the percentage applies to the employee's payable (post-LOP, prorated) amount of the chosen basis for that run; basis CTC means monthly CTC = annual CTC ÷ 12 including employer PF.'
potential_consequence: Test author and implementation pick different readings; the assertion weakens to 'a deduction line exists' and neither test can be called wrong from the contract.
consumer: CAP-6 percentage-head fixture test; CAP-3 gross/deduction assertions with LOP
evidence: SPEC.md CAP-6 lists three bases with no run-time definition; research dim 1 defines CTC as annual only

trigger_condition: No rounding or precision rule exists anywhere in the SPEC; calendar-days divisor in a 31-day month produces non-terminating paise; 'exactly half' flips on rounding order — the research flagged rounding order as a decision to make explicitly and the SPEC dropped it.
guard_snippet: One global line: 'All money is 2 decimal places; per-day wage = monthly amount ÷ divisor, unrounded intermediate, round half-up at the final line amount; a half-day is 0.5 × the per-day wage rounded once at the line.' Also choose CAP-4 fixtures so the three conventions cannot coincide (avoid 30-day months for calendar-vs-fixed-30).
potential_consequence: Two implementations both pass 'distinct arithmetic' and 'exactly half' while producing different payslip paise; the CAP-4 distinctness assertion can degenerate in a 30-day month.
consumer: every money assertion in the payroll suite (CAP-3 gross/LOP/net, CAP-4, CAP-5, CAP-6)
evidence: grep shows no rounding/precision wording in SPEC.md; research dim 3 explicitly says rounding order is a design decision to make explicitly

trigger_condition: 'Payable days from the later of joining/month-start to the earlier of exit/month-end' defines the window but not the numerator: calendar span (week-offs/holidays inside paid) or working days only? Also undefined: does LOP compose inside the window, and can the result exceed the monthly amount?
guard_snippet: State: 'payable days = calendar days in the join/exit window; week-offs and public holidays inside the window are paid days; unpaid-LOP days inside the window subtract; daily wage = the company's divisor; prorated earnings never exceed the month's structure amount.'
potential_consequence: The flagship auto-proration claim ships with whichever numerator the implementer guessed; a working-days-only reading short-changes joiners on week-offs and no acceptance fails.
consumer: CAP-3 proration fixture test and join/exit legs of the payroll journey
evidence: SPEC.md CAP-3 fixes window and divisor but not numerator; the week-offs-paid invariant (constraints) predates and does not reference the proration sentence

trigger_condition: Half-days exist through two sources — leave_requests.part first/second-half AND attendance_day_overrides.status = half_day (owner correction) — and the run consumes the engine 'including owner corrections'; the success tests only the leave path, so the corrected-half-day path into LOP has no acceptance.
guard_snippet: Add the leg: owner corrects a present day to half_day via attendance_day_overrides, then the run yields exactly 0.5 LOP day; reword success to 'an approved half-day leave or an owner-corrected half_day day-status yields exactly half the single-day LOP deduction.'
potential_consequence: A run that reads only leave_requests.part passes every CAP-5 acceptance while overpaying every owner-corrected half-day — the day-status seam the run is mandated to consume is the one left unverified.
consumer: the run's day-status consumption (src/common/day-status: half_day + corrected markers; monthly-summary.model.ts already credits half=0.5)
evidence: code-audit §B documents half-day living twice; SPEC constraint mandates consuming the engine including corrections; CAP-5 success names only the leave path

location: Constraints: 50% cap / formula cycles / idempotent re-run / statutory effective dating
trigger_condition: Testable acceptance lives only in CAP success lines and none of these constraint behaviours appears in any: the cap breach outcome (reject/clamp/recovery record — undefined), cycle rejection at save, re-run idempotency (does an off-cycle line survive a re-run?), effective-dated rate changes.
guard_snippet: One acceptance each: (a) fixture where PT+PF+TDS+LOP exceed 50% — assert the defined breach outcome; (b) save A→B→A formula chain — assert rejection names the chain; (c) run → add off-cycle → re-run — assert payslip count still 1 and state the off-cycle expectation; (d) change a rate's effective date — assert next run uses it, locked month keeps old. Home each in a CAP success (cap→CAP-6, cycles→CAP-2, idempotency→CAP-3, dating→CAP-6/4) or an acceptance appendix.
potential_consequence: The legal and integrity load-bearing walls get no story-level review; the CoW cap (the one statutory rule marked 'CHANGES DESIGN') can ship silently unenforced; a re-run double-counting off-cycle lines passes every written test.
consumer: run engine (cap + idempotency), component-library save path (cycles), statutory-config table (effective dating)
evidence: line-by-line pass of CAP-1..12 success lines finds no reference to cap, cycle rejection, re-run idempotency, or rate effective-dating; statutory digest Q4 verdict CHANGES DESIGN

trigger_condition: 'Rejected with a clear error' names no code (an assertion can only check status ≠ 2xx; 'clear' is human-only) and 'visible in the admin UI' has no automated verification path (fenzit-web has jest-only tests, no e2e driver); the blocked-operation set is open ('edit' of what?).
guard_snippet: Replace with named codes: expect(res.status).toBe(409) + body.code 'PAYROLL_MONTH_LOCKED' for each enumerated blocked operation (re-run, payslip edit, off-cycle into the month, head edit affecting the month); replace UI visibility with 'the month-status API returns locked:true (web renders it)' — API-observable.
potential_consequence: An implementation rejecting with a bare 500 passes the lock test; the web lock badge is checked by nobody — the admin discovers the lock only by a failed run after the month is frozen.
consumer: CAP-9 acceptance test and the fenzit-web admin surface (no payroll feature dir, no web e2e exists)
evidence: verified test infra: fenzit-be jest-e2e real-DB suites; fenzit-web jest-only; code-audit §F confirms web has no payroll dir

location: CAP-10 vs CAP-9 (off-cycle targeting a locked month)
trigger_condition: CAP-10 lets the admin target 'a chosen month' without excluding locked months; the constraints say post-lock corrections go to a LATER month; three contradictory expectations are defensible (rejected / deferred / own payslip) — a test cannot decide which to assert.
guard_snippet: State it: 'an off-cycle targets the current open month or a later unlocked month; targeting a locked month is rejected with PAYROLL_MONTH_LOCKED' (or state deferral semantics); test: run → lock → POST off-cycle targeting locked month → expect 409.
potential_consequence: The off-cycle-vs-lock interaction is where money is double-paid or silently dropped, and it is the one interaction the contract leaves ambiguous; whichever ships, the story author's test blesses it.
consumer: CAP-10 acceptance and CAP-9 lock test — same journey leg asserted differently depending on which clause was read

trigger_condition: Three undecidable assertions: (a) 'beyond paid entitlement' — entitlement numbers are configured by no capability (fixture expected value depends on an undefined number); (b) absence with no leave request (day-status absent) — LOP or paid? no success line decides; (c) 'reclassifying a type changes only future runs' is ambiguous between later months and re-runs executed later.
